newsitem.title: USA: Paxson nears deal to buy New York TV station.
newsitem.headline: Paxson nears deal to buy New York TV station.

text.p: Media company Paxson Communications Corp. is expected to announce as early as next week that it will buy New York's WBIS television station from ITT Corp. and Dow Jones & Co. Inc. for $250 million, according to sources familiar with the negotiations.
Paxson is working this week to line up definitive financing for the deal. The transaction will not occur unless the financing is in place, the sources said.
"There is a handshake (agreement) for a deal at $250 million," said one source who did not want to be identified.
ITT and Dow Jones jointly bought WBIS for $207 million from the city of New York in 1995. The station's business news and sports format generally has not been well-received.
Dow Jones declined to comment on the sale of WBIS, New York's channel 31.
ITT also declined to comment, although company President Robert Bowman said on a conference call Tuesday that the company had received considerable interest in the station.
Paxson could not be reached for comment. The company owns, operates or is affiliated with 47 television stations and reaches 53.4 million households.
A sale of WBIS would mark the latest move taken by ITT to unload non-core assets as it tries to thwart a $6.5 billion hostile takeover attempt by rival Hilton Hotels Corp.
ITT recently has sold its stake in French telecommunications firm Alcatel Alsthom and announced plans to sell its 50 percent interest in Madison Square Garden to partner Cablevision Systems Corp.
The sources said ITT had been in talks with several potential buyers for the sale of its portion of WBIS when Paxson jumped into those discussions and lobbed a bid for the whole station.
The value of WBIS was solidified when the Supreme Court last month upheld a 1992 law that forces cable television operators to carry local station broadcasts.
For Paxson, the acquisition of a New York station would be a significant move toward its strategy of entering major U.S. markets. The company also owns radio stations, mostly in Florida.
Upon announcing a sale of WBIS, ITT will still have a handful of valuable assets to sell. The company owns an international telephone directories business and an educational services unit.

ITT, which is selling the assets to focus on its core hotel and casino businesses, has not announced what it will do with the proceeds of the asset sales. Many industry experts expect the company to issue a special dividend or institute a stock buyback.
